name: PR Files changed tab renders Smart Diff: groups, collapsed lock file, badge reveal
description: From PR #482, open the Files changed tab (Smart Diff is now the default order) and confirm: the three role groups render (Core/Wiring/Boilerplate, uppercased by CSS text-transform — agent-browser matches innerText); package-lock.json is present but collapsed by design (a boilerplate file always starts collapsed, even with a finding — none here); the split banner is absent (the seeded PR's 285 changed lines / 9 files sit under both too_big thresholds); and clicking src/config.ts's finding badge reveals its CRITICAL line. Model-free: the flow never clicks the per-file ✨ Summarize pill, because deriving a real summary needs a model key and e2e runs without one (same rule 08-pr-intent.flow.json follows for 'Derive intent'). CORRECTED after review: agent-browser's `get count`/`find nth` take a real CSS selector — there is NO `text=` engine on those subcommands (only the separate `find text <value>` locator uses text matching); a prior version of this flow used `text=...` for both absence checks and the badge disambiguation and every one of those three steps was silently vacuous (`get count "text=..."` always returns 0, `find nth N "text=..."` always errors). Verified empirically against a static HTML fixture mirroring this page's real DOM shape (nesting, tag names, no class/id — the same convention this app's inline-styled components use) before shipping the replacement selectors below; see task-9-report.md's fix-round section for the exact commands and output. Every DOM fact a selector below relies on is cited to source: DiffTab.tsx wraps the tab in one <section>, not nested inside any other <section> (grepped repo-wide); GroupSection.tsx wraps each role group in its own <section style={s.group}>, itself only ever nested inside DiffTab's <section> when Smart Diff (not the flat viewer) is showing, and always renders exactly 3 direct <div> children in fixed order (heading, meta, list) before any files; FileCard.tsx's root renders exactly 1 direct child <div> (the header) when collapsed and 2 (header + body) when open; toast.tsx's toast container is the only OTHER role=status region on this whole app (grepped client/src) and is unconditionally mounted (empty, so present but with nothing to show) even with zero toasts, so `[role='status']` counts 1 at rest and 2 only when SplitBanner (the sole other role=status element, and the only one that's conditional) also renders. Assumes a freshly-seeded DB where acme/payments-api (PR #482) is the first repo — guaranteed by e2e-web.yml; run locally via the hermetic stack (see e2e/README.md). NOTE: these selectors are empirically proven against a fixture that mirrors the real markup exactly, not against the live app itself — the live run remains blocked by a pre-existing, out-of-scope Windows execFile bug in e2e/run.ts and (this session) an unrelated Docker Desktop outage; see task-9-report.md.

cmd: Add rate limiting to public API endpoints
steps.label: open the PR row
navigate to the PR detail route
switch to the Files changed tab
diff tab is active in the URL
Smart Diff (not the flat viewer) is the default order
the seeded lock file is present

the split banner is absent — only the always-mounted (empty) toast container carries role=status; a rendered SplitBanner would add a second one (too_big is false for the seeded PR: 285 lines / 9 files, both under threshold)

package-lock.json's diff body is NOT rendered: Boilerplate is the 3rd of 3 GroupSection <section>s (Core/Wiring/Boilerplate, present-only, always in that order); its list div is its 3rd direct <div>; package-lock.json (92+24=116 changed lines, 0 findings) sorts ahead of README.md (6+2=8 lines) as the list's 1st FileCard; a FileCard root has exactly 1 direct child <div> (the header) collapsed, 2 (header+body) open — this counts package-lock.json's own direct <div> children specifically, not a page-wide text search

click src/config.ts's finding badge — Wiring is the 2nd GroupSection <section>; within it, src/config.ts (the sole finding-bearing wiring file) sorts first and its badge <button> is the first button rendered in its header, ahead of its own ✨ Summarize <button> — so index 0 of every <button> nested inside the 2nd nested <section> is exactly this badge, never src/api/users.ts's identically-labelled '1 findings' badge (which sits in the Core section, a different nth-of-type(1) group)
src/config.ts's CRITICAL finding line is now visible
